# My plan for this year

Cotton is what I know. I've been growing it since I was a young woman, my mother grew it before me. On these 20 mu, I don't try anything fancy. I do what works — same as last year, same as the year before, unless something pushes me to change.

It's just me and my old man in the house now, the children are grown and living in town. Two pairs of hands aren't enough for 20 mu of cotton, especially come picking time. So I already know I'll need to call on help — neighbors, relatives, maybe hire some women from the village when the bolls open.

**Planting.** I plant after Grain Rain (谷雨), when the soil is warm enough. If I plant too early and a cold snap comes, the seedlings die and I have to replant — wasted seed, wasted time. Usually that means around April 20 or so. I buy seed from the supply cooperative, the hybrid kind in the sealed bag. Can't save cotton seed, it doesn't come back the same. Before planting I lay down plastic film — it keeps the soil warm and holds the moisture.

**The land.** I hire the tractor man from the village to plow in the spring, about sixty yuan per mu. I can't plow 20 mu by hand, and I don't own the machine.

**Fertilizer.** Before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the 15-15-15 kind, 40 kg bag. Then when the cotton is setting bolls, around mid-July, I spread half a bag of urea per mu — maybe 15 kg. That's what I've always done. My neighbor on the east side uses more, she says she gets more cotton, but her land is different from mine, and more fertilizer costs money. I stick with what I know.

**Water.** I have the well, so water is there, but pumping costs money — the electricity meter doesn't lie. I irrigate once right after planting so the seeds come up well, and once again when the bolls are setting and the weather is hot and dry. Two times is usually enough. If the rains come good in summer, maybe just once.

**Pests.** Cotton has many enemies. The bollworm, the aphids, the red spider. I spray when I see them. Usually three or four times across the season. Before planting I also use weedkiller under the plastic film. The sprays cost a lot but if the bollworm gets in, half the crop is gone.

**Picking.** This is the hard part. From mid-September through October, the bolls open in waves, and we pick and pick and pick. The first picking is the best cotton, highest grade. Me and my old man pick what we can, but for 20 mu I need to hire four or five women for three or four weeks, paying by the day. This is where most of my money goes.

**What I expect.** A normal year, I get about 250 kg of lint per mu. A good year, maybe 280. A bad year with bollworm or a typhoon-like wind in August, could drop to 180. I hope for normal.
